_about: The Hermetic writings in English: John David Chambers's Theological and Philosophical Works of Hermes Trismegistus, translated from the Greek (T. & T. Clark, 1882), and John Everard's Divine Pymander (1650), in George Redway's 1884 reprint with Hargrave Jennings's introduction. Raw IA OCR. Not minted. Also G. R. S. Mead's Thrice-Greatest Hermes (Theosophical Publishing Society, 1906), all three volumes: his translation with prolegomena and commentary.

hermetica-chambers-1882: The Theological and Philosophical Works of Hermes Trismegistus, Christian Neoplatonist, translated from the original Greek, with preface, notes and indices (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 1882)
hermetica-everard-pymander-1884: The Divine Pymander of Hermes Mercurius Trismegistus (Everard's translation of 1650; London: George Redway, 1884, with an introduction by Hargrave Jennings)
hermetica-mead-1906-v1: Thrice-Greatest Hermes: Studies in Hellenistic Theosophy and Gnosis, being a translation of the extant sermons and fragments of the Trismegistic literature, vol. I: Prolegomena (London and Benares: Theosophical Publishing Society, 1906)
hermetica-mead-1906-v2: Thrice-Greatest Hermes: Studies in Hellenistic Theosophy and Gnosis, being a translation of the extant sermons and fragments of the Trismegistic literature, vol. II: Sermons (London and Benares: Theosophical Publishing Society, 1906)
hermetica-mead-1906-v3: Thrice-Greatest Hermes: Studies in Hellenistic Theosophy and Gnosis, being a translation of the extant sermons and fragments of the Trismegistic literature, vol. III: Excerpts and Fragments (London and Benares: Theosophical Publishing Society, 1906)

_excluded.Walter Scott, Hermetica (Clarendon, 1924: vol. I (1924, IA ScottHermeticaVolOne) is the only volume with the translation, and it prints the Greek and Latin texts facing; its OCR reads 0.761 clean words, below the lane's bar, mixed with Greek. Vols. II-III (1925-26) are commentary, vol. IV (1936) not public domain. Not taken
